title: How to make $5k+ selling AI-made product demo videos with Claude Code and Remotion
summary: Priyam Raj spots a new trend (Claude Code plus Remotion generating product demo videos by prompt) and turns it into a cold-outreach offer: build a short sample demo for a SaaS founder, then sell the full version for about $1,000. He also argues for chasing short-lived internet opportunities instead of optimizing for stable monthly cash flow.

principles.text: Everything on the internet runs on trends; ride a new launch early to make money.
principles.quote: as someone who has made more than a million dollars on the internet, the way I perceive this whole thing is everything is based on a trend.

principles.text: When AI collapses the cost of a skilled service (animated demos), sell that service to buyers who used to pay specialists.
principles.quote: Back then, it was used to be done by, you know, these professional designers who knew After Effects, Premiere Pro and all that stuff. But um as of today, you can now do this with AI and uh it's very easy to do.

principles.text: Lead with proof: make a short sample for the prospect, then offer the full version at a fixed price via a payment link.
principles.quote: make a product video using cloud code and reotion, a very simple one. cut it out. You know, just give them the first 30 seconds or something

principles.text: Scale the offer through volume outreach: pitch dozens of SaaS companies and expect enough to convert.
principles.quote: And do that to like 50 50 SAS companies, 50 apps. And I can assure you if you plan it plan this whole thing well a lot of people are going to pay for this.

principles.text: Founders and product managers buy on results, so cold email and Twitter DMs work for a deliverable-first offer.
principles.quote: just cold email companies reach out to them on Twitter uh and so many so many corporate founders um or product managers and stuff would 100% be interested cuz they just care about the results and uh nothing else.

principles.text: Don't demand durable cash flow from every opportunity; a short-lived trend that pays well is worth taking, then move on.
principles.quote: if there's a lot of money you can make out of something, why not do it? Like why does everything have to be thought in terms of monthly cash flow?
